evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode="batched" with aggregation="weighted_mean" (functional/judge.toml:3,21; polish/judge.toml:3,15; visual/judge.toml:3,15) and each prompt carries the independence-and-continue instruction. functional/prompt.md:11 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session.', reinforced by :10 'a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed', :15 'stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest', :26 'give every criterion its own verdict', :27 'fail that criterion and move on'. polish/prompt.md:10 has the same sentence, plus :11 'Never carry a verdict across criteria ... Attempt every criterion' and :20 'fail that criterion and move on'. visual/prompt.md:13 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any low score; return a score for every criterion. Give every criterion its own observation and never carry a score across criteria.' and :21 '...and move on'. No scored prompt tells the judge to stop at the first failure: the only 'stop' in the prompts (functional/prompt.md:15) is scoped to one criterion and immediately followed by 'continue with the rest'. A scan of all 49 scored criterion texts found no stop-the-session, fail-all or inherit-another-criterion wording and no criterion id referenced from another criterion; the single hit, in cw_output_before_failure_kept ('scored by other criteria, not here'), narrows scope rather than coupling verdicts. The only zero-all clause is the template-mandated global browser gate at line 5 of each prompt, which matches the frozen template functional/prompt.md:9-13 and is a precondition, not a first-failure stop. Gate dimensions (all_pass, gates/*/judge.toml:15) are exempt. Broken-app probe: an app failing the first functional criterion still gets the other 39 graded under :11. Conforming-alternative probe: no instruction lets one miss fail a sibling. Limits: this is a source reading; the private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed, and no configured judge run exists to show the judge actually returns 49 verdicts after a failure (the raw evidence index is scripted golden evidence only). Minor observation, not a defect: visual/prompt.md:13 says 'low score' rather than 'failure', which is the accurate word for a 0-5 Likert dimension but differs from the checker's documented phrase; the deterministic reviewer should confirm that row.
